drafts.text: H‑Net’s routing module measures cosine similarity between adjacent encoder output vectors to detect contextual shifts [2]. It projects the encoder outputs \(\hat X\) into queries \(q_t = W_q \hat x_t\) and keys \(k_{t-1} = W_k \hat x_{t-1}\) and computes a boundary probability \(p_t = \tfrac12\bigl[1 - \frac{q_t^\top k_{t-1}}{\|q_t\|\|k_{t-1}\|}\bigr]\) which lies in \([0,1]\) [2]. A hard boundary indicator \(b_t\) is set to 1 when \(p_t \ge 0.5\), i.e., \(b_t = \mathbf{1}_{p_t \ge 0.5}\) [2].
H‑Net can reach comparable DNA modeling performance using only about one‑third of the data that isotropic models require, i.e., it is roughly 3.6 × more data‑efficient than isotropic models【3】.
